note: THE ROADMAP, beside the code it plans, so that the people and the agents working on the engine plan from it. Each item has an id, a name, one line on what it does, and a state - next or later - and may link the issue it answers (`issue`) and say who asked for it there (`asked_by`, a GitHub login). It is a file, not a tracker, because a file is diffed, gated and read by a build with no token: the company's site copies it and holds the copy with `wherefore check upstream`, so what the site says is coming is what is written here. An item leaves in the same change that ships it: tests/test_roadmap.py fails an item whose id src/wherefore/features.json already has. Requests arrive as issues; an item here may name the one it answers.

items.name: Drift, on the map
items.words: What the scan finds - a value stated in several places that no source holds - drawn on the map beside the files that say it, so what is not yet tracked is seen, and seen shrinking.

items.name: Your things, in one place
items.words: An app you log in to and see every repository you connected: what each builds, what is held, and what is drifting.
